title: Joshua Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 11.

questions.question: Who did Jabin king of Hazor send messages to after hearing the news?
options: Jobab king of Madon, king of Shimron, king of Achshaph
Joshua and the children of Israel
The Amorite and the Hittite kings
questions.correctAnswer: Jobab king of Madon, king of Shimron, king of Achshaph
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:1 states that Jabin king of Hazor sent to Jobab king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph after hearing those things.

questions.question: Where were the kings located that Jabin sent messages to besides Madon, Shimron, and Achshaph?
options: On the north of the mountains, plains south of Chinneroth, valley, and borders of Dor on the west
questions.correctAnswer: On the north of the mountains, plains south of Chinneroth, valley, and borders of Dor on the west
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:2 describes the kings as those on the north of the mountains, of the plains south of Chinneroth, in the valley, and in the borders of Dor on the west.

questions.question: Which peoples did Jabin also send messages to that lived on both east and west?
options: Canaanite, Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Jebusite, Hivite
questions.correctAnswer: Canaanite, Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Jebusite, Hivite
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:3 lists the Canaanite on the east and west, Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Jebusite in the mountains, and Hivite under Hermon in Mizpeh as those sent messages.

questions.question: How did the assembled hosts compare in number?
options: As the sand upon the sea shore in multitude
Like the stars in the sky
Only a small band of warriors
questions.correctAnswer: As the sand upon the sea shore in multitude
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:4 describes the multitude as being like the sand upon the sea shore, indicating a very large number.

questions.question: Where did all these kings gather to fight against Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: At the waters of Merom
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:5 states that the kings met together and pitched at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Joshua to do about the horses and chariots of the enemy?
options: Hough their horses and burn their chariots with fire
Take the horses and chariots as spoils
Leave the horses and chariots untouched
Use their horses and chariots against them
questions.correctAnswer: Hough their horses and burn their chariots with fire
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:6 records the LORD's command to Joshua to hough the horses and burn the chariots with fire.

questions.question: How did Joshua approach the enemy at the waters of Merom?
options: Suddenly with all the people of war
questions.correctAnswer: Suddenly with all the people of war
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:7 says Joshua came with all the people of war suddenly against them by the waters of Merom.

questions.question: Where did Israel chase the defeated kings after the battle?
options: Great Zidon, Misrephothmaim, valley of Mizpeh eastward
questions.correctAnswer: Great Zidon, Misrephothmaim, valley of Mizpeh eastward
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:8 states Israel chased the defeated kings unto great Zidon, Misrephothmaim, and the valley of Mizpeh eastward.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD told Joshua to be afraid because the enemy had many horses and chariots.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:6 says the LORD told Joshua not to be afraid because He would deliver the enemy into Israel's hand.

questions.question: True or False: The enemies of Israel came from both the mountains and the plains.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:2-3 shows kings from the mountains and plains, confirming enemies came from both regions.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua fought the battle at the waters of Merom after a long delay.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:7 says he came suddenly with all the people of war against the enemy at the waters of Merom.

questions.question: True or False: The number of people that came against Israel was compared to the sand on the sea shore.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:4 compares the multitude of enemies to the sand upon the sea shore in multitude.

questions.question: Which group is NOT mentioned as being sent a message by Jabin king of Hazor?
questions.correctAnswer: Philistines
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:3 lists the groups sent messages but does not mention the Philistines.

questions.question: What was the LORD's promise to Joshua regarding the battle against the kings at Merom?
options: He would deliver all slain before Israel
He would cause the enemy to flee without fighting
He would send a plague among the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: He would deliver all slain before Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:6 records the LORD's promise to deliver all the enemy slain before Israel.

questions.question: In what order did these events happen according to Joshua 11:1-8?
options: Jabin sends messages; kings gather; LORD commands Joshua; battle at Merom; Israel chases enemies
Battle at Merom; kings gather; Jabin sends messages; Israel chases enemies; LORD commands Joshua
Kings gather; Jabin sends messages; battle at Merom; LORD commands Joshua; Israel chases enemies
Israel chases enemies; LORD commands Joshua; battle at Merom; kings gather; Jabin sends messages
questions.correctAnswer: Jabin sends messages; kings gather; LORD commands Joshua; battle at Merom; Israel chases enemies
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:1-8 shows the sequence starting with Jabin sending messages, kings gathering, LORD commanding Joshua, battle at Merom, and Israel chasing the enemies.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What specific action did Joshua take against the horses and chariots after the battle, as commanded by the LORD?
options: He fed the horses and repaired the chariots
He hough their horses and burnt their chariots with fire
He sold the horses and kept the chariots
He ignored the horses and chariots
questions.correctAnswer: He hough their horses and burnt their chariots with fire
questions.explanation: Joshua obeyed the LORD's command to disable the enemy's military power by hamstringing their horses and burning their chariots, as stated explicitly in Joshua 11:9. This shows his strict obedience to God's instructions (Joshua 11:6, Joshua 11:9).

questions.question: Which city did Joshua capture and burn that was known as the head of all those kingdoms?
questions.correctAnswer: Hazor
questions.explanation: Joshua took Hazor, the leading city among the kingdoms, smote its king, and burnt the city with fire as a demonstration of total conquest (Joshua 11:10-11).

questions.question: According to Joshua 11, how did Joshua deal with the souls in Hazor after capturing it?
options: He spared the women and children
He smote all the souls with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them
He made a treaty with them
questions.correctAnswer: He smote all the souls with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them
questions.explanation: Joshua executed the LORD’s command to utterly destroy all inhabitants in Hazor, leaving none alive, as a fulfillment of divine judgment (Joshua 11:11, Joshua 11:12).

questions.question: What did Joshua do with the cities that stood strong, other than Hazor?
options: He destroyed none of them except Hazor
He destroyed some but spared most
questions.correctAnswer: He destroyed none of them except Hazor
questions.explanation: Joshua did not burn any other strong cities besides Hazor, indicating selective destruction as commanded by the LORD (Joshua 11:13).

questions.question: What did the children of Israel take as spoil after the conquest of the cities?
options: The spoil of the cities and the cattle
Only the children of the kings
questions.correctAnswer: The spoil of the cities and the cattle
questions.explanation: After utterly destroying the inhabitants, Israel took the spoil and cattle as their prey, following the LORD’s instructions (Joshua 11:14).

questions.question: How does Joshua 11:15 show the importance of obedience in leadership?
options: By stating Joshua ignored Moses' commands
By saying Joshua fulfilled all the LORD's commands given through Moses
By emphasizing Joshua’s personal ideas over Moses’
questions.correctAnswer: By saying Joshua fulfilled all the LORD's commands given through Moses
questions.explanation: Joshua’s complete obedience to what the LORD commanded Moses reflects the biblical principle that faithful leadership involves following God’s instructions fully (Joshua 11:15).

questions.question: Which regions did Joshua take possession of after the battle, according to Joshua 11:16?
options: The hills, south country, land of Goshen, valley, plain, and mountains of Israel
Only the valley of the same
questions.correctAnswer: The hills, south country, land of Goshen, valley, plain, and mountains of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua’s conquest was comprehensive, taking possession of all these diverse regions, showing the fulfillment of God’s promise to give Israel the land (Joshua 11:16).

questions.question: How does Joshua 11:10-11 demonstrate the principle of complete obedience to God's commands?
options: Joshua spared many cities, showing mercy
Joshua partially obeyed by capturing but not burning Hazor
Joshua utterly destroyed Hazor and its king as God commanded
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua utterly destroyed Hazor and its king as God commanded
questions.explanation: Joshua’s complete destruction of Hazor and its king illustrates his full obedience to God’s command, fulfilling divine judgment without compromise (Joshua 11:10-11).

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 11:12, Joshua spared some kings and cities after the conquest as an act of mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua did not spare any kings or cities; he utterly destroyed them as commanded by Moses and the LORD (Joshua 11:12).

questions.question: What lesson about faith and trust in God can be learned from Joshua 11:9 and Joshua 11:15?
options: Trust in human strength is most important
Obedience to God's commands leads to victory and fulfillment of His promises
Ignoring God's commands sometimes works better
Partial obedience is sufficient for success
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commands leads to victory and fulfillment of His promises
questions.explanation: Joshua's obedience in disabling the horses and burning chariots (Joshua 11:9) and fulfilling all commands (Joshua 11:15) teaches that trusting and obeying God fully results in success and blessings.

questions.question: What does Joshua 11:13 reveal about the nature of God's judgment and mercy regarding the cities that stood strong?
options: All strong cities were destroyed without exception
Only Hazor was burned, indicating selective judgment
Joshua chose which cities to burn based on their size
questions.correctAnswer: Only Hazor was burned, indicating selective judgment
questions.explanation: God’s judgment was precise; only Hazor, the head city, was burned while others that stood strong were spared from burning, showing measured divine justice (Joshua 11:13).

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 11:14 teaches that after obeying God's command to destroy the inhabitants, the Israelites were allowed to take the spoils and cattle for themselves.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that the children of Israel took all the spoil and cattle for themselves after smiting all the inhabitants, illustrating obedience with provision (Joshua 11:14).

questions.question: How does Joshua 11:16-17 emphasize God's faithfulness in fulfilling His promises to Israel?
options: By describing Joshua's failure to conquer all the land
By detailing Joshua's full conquest and taking all the lands and kings as God commanded
By showing Joshua’s reluctance to fight
questions.correctAnswer: By detailing Joshua's full conquest and taking all the lands and kings as God commanded
questions.explanation: These verses affirm that Joshua took all the land and defeated all the kings, fulfilling the LORD’s promises given through Moses, demonstrating God’s faithfulness (Joshua 11:16-17).

questions.question: Why did Joshua burn Hazor alone among the cities, according to Joshua 11:13 and its surrounding context?
options: Because it was the strongest city
Because it was the head of all the kingdoms and a symbol of opposition
Because the people of Hazor surrendered
Because it was located near the sea
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was the head of all the kingdoms and a symbol of opposition
questions.explanation: Joshua burned Hazor alone as it was the chief city leading the opposition, showing the significance of removing the primary source of rebellion (Joshua 11:10-13).

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 11:15 states that Joshua left some of the LORD’s commands undone after the conquest.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that Joshua left nothing undone of all that the LORD commanded Moses, showing complete obedience (Joshua 11:15).

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 11.

questions.question: From which locations did Joshua cut off the Anakims according to Joshua 11?
options: Hebron, Debir, Anab, mountains of Judah and Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Hebron, Debir, Anab, mountains of Judah and Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:21 specifically mentions that Joshua cut off the Anakims from Hebron, Debir, Anab, and all the mountains of Judah and Israel.

questions.question: Which cities still had Anakims remaining after Joshua's campaign?
questions.correctAnswer: Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:22 states that only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did Anakims remain after the campaign.

questions.question: What was the ultimate outcome of Joshua's conquest according to Joshua 11:23?
options: The land was taken and given as an inheritance to Israel, and the land rested from war
The land was divided among the kings defeated by Joshua
Joshua returned to Egypt after the conquest
The Israelites made peace with all the cities
questions.correctAnswer: The land was taken and given as an inheritance to Israel, and the land rested from war
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:23 explains that Joshua took the whole land as the LORD commanded Moses, distributed it as inheritance, and the land rested from war.

questions.question: What geographical extent of the land did Joshua take according to Joshua 11:17?
options: From mount Halak to Baalgad in the valley of Lebanon under mount Hermon
From the Red Sea to the Dead Sea
questions.correctAnswer: From mount Halak to Baalgad in the valley of Lebanon under mount Hermon
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:17 states that Joshua took the land from mount Halak going up to Seir to Baalgad in the valley of Lebanon under mount Hermon.

questions.question: Which city was the only one Joshua burned during his campaign?
questions.correctAnswer: Hazor
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:13 clarifies that the only city Joshua burned was Hazor.

questions.question: According to Joshua 11:19, which inhabitants made peace with Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: The Hivites of Gibeon
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:19 states that no city made peace with Israel except the Hivites who lived in Gibeon.

questions.question: What was the reason given in Joshua 11:20 for the kings coming against Israel in battle?
options: The LORD hardened their hearts so they would be destroyed as commanded
They sought to make peace but were rejected
They wanted to form an alliance with Israel
They were deceived by false prophets
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD hardened their hearts so they would be destroyed as commanded
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:20 explains that it was the LORD's will to harden the kings' hearts to bring about their destruction as He commanded Moses.

questions.question: Joshua made war a long time with all the kings according to which verse?
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua 11:18
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:18 states explicitly that Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book details the command to utterly destroy the Canaanite cities, which Joshua fulfilled in chapter 11?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:12 and 11:15 show that Joshua followed the commands given to Moses, which are detailed in Deuteronomy regarding destruction of the Canaanite cities.

questions.question: The word 'houghed' used in Joshua 11:9 means:
options: To disable by cutting the legs
questions.correctAnswer: To disable by cutting the legs
questions.explanation: In Joshua 11:9, 'houghed' refers to the disabling of horses by cutting their legs to prevent their use in battle.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the structure of Joshua 11, where the narrative begins and ends with the taking of the land and rest from war?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The chapter opens with Joshua's conquest and closes with the land resting from war (Joshua 11:1 and 11:23), demonstrating an inclusio framing device.

questions.question: According to Joshua 11:16, which regions of the land did Joshua take?
options: Hills, south country, land of Goshen, valley, plain, mountain and valley of Israel
Only the plains near the Jordan River
Only the mountainous regions of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Hills, south country, land of Goshen, valley, plain, mountain and valley of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:16 lists these as the regions Joshua took during his conquest.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 11:20, the hardening of the kings' hearts was contrary to the LORD's will.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:20 states that it was the LORD's will to harden their hearts so they would come against Israel and be destroyed, showing it was according to His plan.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua completely destroyed all the Anakims in the land of Israel except those in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:21-22 confirms that Joshua cut off the Anakims utterly except those remaining in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God hardening hearts, as seen in Joshua 11:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 9:17-18
questions.explanation: Romans 9:17-18 discusses God hardening Pharaoh's heart to display His power, paralleling the theme of divine hardening in Joshua 11:20.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by His command to Joshua to 'hough their horses, and burn their chariots with fire'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:6 shows God's justice as He commands the destruction of horses and chariots to prevent future warfare against Israel, demonstrating righteous judgment against enemies.

questions.question: What does the complete destruction of Hazor, including burning the city and killing all souls therein, signify doctrinally?
options: The doctrine of salvation by works
The doctrine of human free will
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine judgment
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:11 describes the utter destruction of Hazor, illustrating God's judgment on persistent sin and rebellion against Him.

questions.question: How does Joshua 11:15 emphasize the doctrine of obedience in the life of God's servant?
options: Joshua ignored some of God's commands
Joshua left nothing undone of what God commanded
Joshua modified the commands to suit his judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua left nothing undone of what God commanded
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:15 highlights complete obedience to God's instructions, affirming the importance of faithful submission to divine authority.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Joshua 11:18 and Joshua 11:19 convey about the nature of Israel's conquest?
options: The conquest was effortless and peaceful
The conquest was prolonged and involved both war and peace
The conquest was conducted without any battles
The conquest was only spiritual, not physical
questions.correctAnswer: The conquest was prolonged and involved both war and peace
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:18 speaks of long-lasting war with the kings, while 11:19 notes that only the Hivites of Gibeon made peace, showing a mix of warfare and diplomacy.

questions.question: In what way does Joshua 11:20 reveal God's sovereign control over human hearts in the context of judgment?
options: God allows humans to act without influence
God hardens hearts to bring about His judgment
God always softens hearts for repentance
God is indifferent to human decisions
questions.correctAnswer: God hardens hearts to bring about His judgment
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:20 states the LORD hardened the hearts of kings so they would fight Israel, demonstrating God's sovereignty even over human will in judgment.

questions.question: What theological significance does the complete extermination of the Anakims, except in certain cities, hold in Joshua 11:21-22?
options: It demonstrates God's judgment on giants and enemy strongholds
It indicates God's failure to fully deliver the land
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God's judgment on giants and enemy strongholds
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:21-22 records the destruction of the Anakims, emphasizing God's power to remove formidable enemies as part of His redemptive plan.

questions.question: How does Joshua 11:23 contribute to the biblical narrative of God's promise and fulfillment regarding the Promised Land?
options: Joshua failed to take the land as promised
The land was taken and divided as the LORD commanded Moses
The land was given to foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: The land was taken and divided as the LORD commanded Moses
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:23 shows the fulfillment of God's covenant promises to Israel by fully taking and dividing the land among the tribes.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Joshua 11:8 where the LORD delivers Israel's enemies into their hands?
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:8 emphasizes God's providential care in granting Israel victory by delivering their enemies completely into their hands.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by Joshua's complete destruction of the cities and kings as Moses commanded in Joshua 11:12?
options: The doctrine of holy war (herem) as divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of holy war (herem) as divine judgment
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:12 reflects the concept of herem, the complete dedication of enemies to God’s judgment, illustrating divine justice and holiness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's command to utterly destroy cities contradicts the character of a loving God. What does Joshua 11:10-11 actually teach about God's holiness and justice?
options: God is indifferent to sin and allows it to continue
God executes righteous judgment on persistent evil
God punishes without reason or justice
questions.correctAnswer: God executes righteous judgment on persistent evil
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:10-11 shows God’s holiness demanding judgment against sin, emphasizing that His justice requires the removal of persistent rebellion against His covenant.

questions.question: What theological insight arises from comparing Joshua 11:13 and Joshua 11:11 regarding the treatment of cities during the conquest?
options: Only Hazor was burned because it was the head of the kingdoms
No city was destroyed by fire
Hazor was spared because of its importance
questions.correctAnswer: Only Hazor was burned because it was the head of the kingdoms
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:13 contrasts with 11:11 showing that while many cities were destroyed, only Hazor was burned, indicating its unique status and symbolic destruction of leadership.

questions.question: How does the alliance of multiple kings against Israel in Joshua 11:1-4 contribute to the understanding of human opposition to God's purposes?
options: Human opposition is weak and insignificant
Human opposition is often united but ultimately defeated by God
God encourages human alliances against His people
questions.correctAnswer: Human opposition is often united but ultimately defeated by God
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:1-4 shows a coalition of kings opposing Israel, typifying human resistance to God's plan, which God sovereignly overcomes.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's faithfulness to His promises is expressed in Joshua 11:16-17 concerning the extent of the land taken?
options: God’s promises can be partially fulfilled
God fully grants the land promised to Israel
God’s promises were ignored by Joshua
God’s promises were conditional on Israel’s failure
questions.correctAnswer: God fully grants the land promised to Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:16-17 details the full extent of the land taken, confirming God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His covenant promises to Israel.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Joshua 11:14 and Joshua 11:15 provide regarding the spoils and judgment in Israel's conquest?
options: Israel shared the spoils with remaining enemies
Israel took spoils but utterly destroyed the enemies as commanded
Israel spared many enemies and took no spoil
Israel disobeyed God's command concerning the spoils
questions.correctAnswer: Israel took spoils but utterly destroyed the enemies as commanded
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:14-15 teaches that Israel claimed the spoil yet executed complete destruction of their enemies, illustrating obedience mixed with provision.

questions.question: How does the account of the kings gathering at the waters of Merom in Joshua 11:5-7 illustrate God's providential care in the battle?
options: God was unaware of the battle plans
God orchestrated a sudden attack that led to Israel's victory
God allowed the kings to win
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrated a sudden attack that led to Israel's victory
questions.explanation: Joshua 11:5-7 narrates the kings assembling, but God commands Joshua to attack suddenly, demonstrating divine providence in securing victory.
